name: From Experience to Strategy: Empowering LLM Agents with Trainable Graph Memory (trainable multi-layered graph memory of decision paths + meta-cognition; sometimes referred to internally as 'Graph Memory / strategy graph')
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2511.07800, cs.CL), submitted 11 Nov 2025 (v1). DBLP: journals/corr/abs-2511-07800. No peer-reviewed venue confirmed as of the snapshot; listed under 'Agent Memory' research on the corresponding author's homepage but without a published-venue tag.
authors_affiliation: Siyu Xia (co-first; Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CASIA) & School of AI, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Zekun Xu (co-first; Meituan), Jiajun Chai (Meituan), Wentian Fan (Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications), Yan Song (AI Centre, Dept. of Computer Science, University College London), Xiaohan Wang (Meituan), Guojun Yin (Meituan; corresponding-affiliated), Wei Lin (Meituan), Haifeng Zhang (corresponding; CASIA & UCAS, haifeng.zhang@ia.ac.cn), Jun Wang (corresponding; UCL, jun.wang@cs.ucl.ac.uk). Primary affiliations: Chinese Academy of Sciences / UCAS, Meituan, and University College London.
code_url: N/A (no official code release found; the corresponding author's homepage gjyin.github.io lists the work under 'Agent Memory: Graph Memory (strategy graph)' but the associated code/project links resolve to a placeholder anchor 'gjyin.github.io/#'. The paper does not provide a repository link. Built on the public RL-Factory framework https://github.com/Simple-Efficient/RL-Factory and the Search-R1 setup, but these are dependencies, not the method's own released code.) [uncertain]
task_domain: Tool-augmented / agentic question answering and decision-making: open-domain factoid QA and multi-hop QA solved by an LLM agent that interleaves reasoning (<think>) with retrieval tool calls (<tool_call> over a Wikipedia RAG MCP tool) and answer generation (<answer>). Framed as long-horizon strategic tool-use / decision-making for LLM agents.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent, multi-turn tool-integrated decision process formalized as s_t=(q, h_{1:t-1}), a_t ~ pi_theta(a_t|s_t), with actions being internal reasoning, a tool (RAG search) call, or answer generation, up to K=6 tool invocations. Two regimes are studied: (1) Direct/zero-training inference (the memory workflow is plugged into a frozen Qwen3 backbone), and (2) RL training, where the structured memory is injected into the GRPO training loop (Search-R1 style) to guide policy optimization. Supervision: outcome reward via Exact Match against ground-truth QA answers (used both to label success/failure trajectories during memory construction and as the RL/counterfactual reward). The central research question is whether dynamic structured EXPLICIT memory can actively guide and enhance IMPLICIT (parametric) policy learning, combining the interpretability of prompting with the generalization of training. Memory is built exclusively from in-domain HotpotQA (1,000 examples for memory construction + 5,000 for graph-weight training; remaining HotpotQA training split used as the RL corpus); evaluation spans 7 QA datasets (HotpotQA in-domain, six out-of-domain). Hardware: 8x A100; vLLM v1; GRPO with n=8 rollouts, batch 512, temperature 1.0.
what_is_retrieved: High-level, human-interpretable strategic 'meta-cognition' nodes (generalized heuristics / decision principles, e.g. 'early recognition of KnowledgeSufficient state and structured validation help prevent synthesis inaccuracies'), distilled from abstracted decision paths. Retrieval is keyed by query similarity and traverses the trainable graph (query -> transition-path -> meta-cognition); the retrieved/injected unit is the top-k meta-cognition strategies (not raw trajectories). Underneath, the graph also stores raw query nodes (with trajectories and outcome labels) and canonical FSM decision-path nodes, but only meta-cognitions are verbalized into the prompt.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / experience-induced memory: the retrievable store is a heterogeneous graph the agent builds from its OWN sampled trajectories on HotpotQA (successful and failed), abstracted via an FSM and distilled into meta-cognitions, with a separate Wikipedia RAG corpus used only as the agent's external tool at solve time. So the STRATEGY memory is a self-written/induced experiential store (constructed offline from training rollouts, then frozen for downstream evaluation/RL), while the factual knowledge access (the search tool over the 2018 Wikipedia dump) is a static external corpus. Net: HYBRID (self-induced strategy graph + static external Wikipedia knowledge tool), with the studied/learned memory being the growing-experience graph.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking objective: a query activates a similarity-based subgraph and the top-k highest-relevance-score meta-cognitions are selected (selection-probability via softmax over learned-weight-aggregated path scores). k is a fixed small hyperparameter (k=3 reported as the best balance in the main text; appendix Table 3 finds top_k=5 marginally best on the 4B average). No minimal-complete-set or variable-size precision-driven objective.
retrieval_unit: guideline-rule / distilled strategic meta-cognition node (a high-level, human-readable problem-solving principle). The graph has three node types: query nodes (task instance + trajectory + outcome), transition-path nodes (canonical FSM decision pathways abstracting raw traces), and meta-cognition nodes (distilled heuristics); the injected retrieval unit is the meta-cognition node.
index_source: Growing memory, offline-induced from training rollouts then frozen for downstream use (hybrid in the broader sense). The strategy graph is constructed before evaluation by sampling N trajectories per query from the policy on HotpotQA, grounding each to an FSM path, and inducing meta-cognitions; graph EDGE WEIGHTS are then trained (Stage 2). At downstream inference/RL the graph is fixed and queried. A static external Wikipedia (2018 dump, E5 retriever) serves as the agent's search tool but is not the strategy index.
index_structure_topology: Dependency / knowledge GRAPH with a hierarchical (multi-layered) topology: a heterogeneous directed acyclic graph G=(V,E,O_V,R_E,C) with three layers Q (query) -> T (transition path) -> M (meta-cognition), connected by bipartite adjacency matrices A^{q->t} and A^{t->m}, each augmented with learnable weights w_qt and w_tm. Transition-path nodes are canonical paths over a finite state machine (FSM) of abstract cognitive states (e.g. StrategyPlanning, InformationAnalysis, ToolExecution, DecisionMaking, DiagnosisHub). Query similarity (cosine over embeddings) activates task-specific subgraphs.
retriever_type: Hybrid: dense embedding similarity (cosine over query embeddings, Sim(q_new,q_i)=cos(e_qnew,e_qi)) to activate the relevant subgraph / find similar historical queries, combined with a LEARNED graph-weight relevance score rho(m_k|q_new)=sum_{q_i,t_j: q_i->t_j->m_k} Sim(q_new,q_i)*w_qt^{(i,j)}*w_tm^{(j,k)} and softmax selection. The graph edge weights are trained by policy gradient (REINFORCE), so the retriever is partly a learned scoring function over a graph, not pure off-the-shelf top-k. (The external factual search tool is a separate E5 dense retriever over Wikipedia.)
retriever_learning_signal: RL / learned-policy via downstream-task effectiveness (counterfactual reward). Stage 2 trains the graph edge weights with REINFORCE: for a sampled meta-cognition m_k, it runs the agent WITH guidance m_k (reward R_with) and WITHOUT (R_w/o), forms the reward gap Delta R_k = R_with - R_w/o (utility signal), and updates weights via L_RL = -E_{m_k~p}[Delta R_k * log p(m_k|q_new)]. Positive Delta R_k strengthens supporting q->t->m paths, negative weakens them. The base query-similarity uses off-the-shelf embeddings, but the utility/relevance calibration is RL-trained on task reward (Exact Match), making this a value/utility-driven learned selection signal.
query_construction: Raw query context: a new query q_new is represented by its embedding similarity to historical query nodes in the graph; the top-k most similar neighbors activate a task-specific subgraph G(q_new)=(Q',T',M'). No query decomposition, intent extraction, or synthetic expansion; the agent additionally issues raw-text search-tool queries during solving (e.g. 'George D. Maziarz state').
query_granularity: task-level (one-shot at t=0): retrieval of meta-cognitions from the graph is performed per incoming query, and the selected strategies are prepended to the query for the whole episode (q_tilde = [m_1,...,m_k; q_train]). The agent's separate factual tool calls happen per-step during the rollout, but the strategy-memory retrieval that this method contributes is task-level.
when_to_retrieve: one-shot (per task): the top-k meta-cognitions are retrieved once from the (optimized) memory graph and prepended to the query before the agent acts; they remain fixed context throughout that episode's reasoning/tool loop.
retrieval_trigger_signal: fixed schedule: strategy retrieval is triggered unconditionally for every query (compute relevance scores for all activated meta-cognitions, take top-k). Within the rollout, the agent itself decides when to call the factual RAG tool (agent-initiated, reasoning-conditioned) but that is the underlying tool-use, not the contributed memory-retrieval trigger.
reranking: Effectively a learned-weight relevance scoring/ranking rather than a separate cross-encoder reranking stage: meta-cognitions are scored by aggregated learned graph-path weights (rho), softmax-normalized, and the top-k are selected. No external cross-encoder, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranker is reported.
retrieved_context_refinement: None beyond selection: retrieved meta-cognitions are verbalized and prepended to the query without post-retrieval compression, decomposition, or distractor filtering. Abstraction/distillation happens at WRITE time (FSM grounding + meta-cognition induction), and the trainable weights act to suppress low-utility strategies; the appendix notes too many strategies can introduce noise/overlap, motivating a small k rather than a refinement module.
how_retrieved_used: Both prompt augmentation AND training signal. (1) Prompt augmentation: top-k meta-cognitions are prepended to the query (q_tilde=[m_1,...,m_k; q]) as an explicit strategic policy prior at inference and during RL rollouts. (2) Training signal: the augmented context is fed to the policy which is then optimized with GRPO (L_{RL+Mem} = -E_{a~pi_theta(.|q_tilde)}[R(a)]), so the memory directly shapes implicit policy learning. The memory graph's own edge weights are also trained via REINFORCE on counterfactual reward. This dual integration into the RL training loop (not inference-only) is the paper's distinguishing claim.
planning_integration: retrieve-then-plan, integrated into the RL training loop: for each training instance, top-k meta-cognitions are retrieved from the optimized graph and prepended to the query; the GRPO policy then plans and acts (multi-turn reasoning + RAG tool calls up to 6) conditioned on these strategic priors, and gradients update the policy. Memory is thus a per-task strategic prior at the start of planning that is woven into RL optimization, rather than per-step interleaving inside a tree search.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer / per-task for the contributed strategy memory (meta-cognitions injected once and held fixed across the episode's reasoning). The underlying agent reasoning interleaves with factual tool calls per-tool-call within the rollout (ReAct-style think/tool_call/tool_response), but the memory-retrieval contribution operates at the per-task level.
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled strategy / free-text guideline: a concise, human-readable strategic principle (meta-cognition) with cautious-language phrasing ('consider', 'may help', 'tends to'), e.g. structured-validation and confidence-awareness heuristics. Internally each meta-cognition node carries summary, strategy_principles with confidence scores (30-85), overall_confidence, evidence_paths count, and an uncertainty_note; the verbalized item prepended to the prompt is the natural-language strategy text. Not a raw trajectory, executable program, or latent token.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled high-level strategy / meta-cognition (the most abstract layer). The pipeline deliberately abstracts raw trajectories -> canonical FSM decision paths (intermediate) -> generalizable meta-cognitive principles (top layer), filtering execution-level noise to preserve only semantically meaningful, transferable decision strategies; these are what get retrieved and injected.
noise_robustness_mechanism: (1) Trainable utility weighting: REINFORCE on counterfactual reward gaps strengthens broadly useful meta-cognitions and suppresses ineffective/overly-specific ones (ablation: freezing weights to uniform significantly degrades performance, especially on 2WikiMultiHopQA). (2) FSM grounding filters execution-level noise so only semantically meaningful decision points are stored. (3) Selective memory update (reinforce/create/skip; discard redundant or low-confidence paths; cap ~30 meta-cognitions, preferring updates over creation). (4) Small k (k=3) to avoid prompt overload / conflicting strategies. (5) Cautious-language prompting and explicit uncertainty acknowledgment in induced strategies to avoid over-confident, misleading heuristics.
memory_type: graph (trainable, multi-layered heterogeneous graph memory) over distilled procedural/strategic knowledge: query layer + canonical-FSM transition-path layer + meta-cognition layer, with learnable edge weights. Combines episodic provenance (query/trajectory nodes) with a procedural/strategy abstraction (meta-cognitions).
write_back: Yes (during memory construction). Algorithm 1 (UpdateMemoryGraph) adds the new query node, samples N trajectories, grounds each to an FSM path node, adds query->path edges, induces meta-cognitions (intra-query contrast of success vs failure, inter-query speculative from similar queries, or positive-example distillation), and creates/updates meta-cognition nodes plus path->meta edges. Writing is part of the (offline) memory-formation phase from training rollouts; the graph is then frozen for downstream evaluation/RL (no further online growth reported at deployment).
online_growth: No (not during downstream deployment/RL): the strategy graph is constructed and weight-trained on HotpotQA rollouts in a dedicated phase, then used as a fixed/optimized memory for evaluation and as a fixed prior during RL training. The construction algorithm itself is incremental/append-and-update per query, but the paper does not grow the graph during the downstream test-time stream.
write_back_trigger: on-success-and-failure, reflective per-query during construction: for each construction query, N trajectories are sampled and labeled success/failure (by Exact Match), then meta-cognitions are induced and the graph updated. Three induction triggers: (Case 1) both success and failure paths exist -> high-confidence causal meta-cognition by contrasting their FSM paths; (Case 2) only failures -> speculative meta-cognitions borrowed from successful paths of top-K semantically similar queries; (else, e.g. only successes / no rollouts in Alg.1) skip, though appendix also describes Positive Example Distillation from successful paths. A new meta-cognition is created if no match exists, else an existing one's confidence is updated.
failure_experience_usage: Success + failure used contrastively (a core design point): high-confidence meta-cognitions are derived by CONTRASTING successful vs failed FSM paths of the same query to explain outcome divergence; failure-only queries trigger speculative heuristics from similar successful queries. Failed paths thus directly drive strategy induction (failure-cause summary / errors-to-avoid), not just success patterns. Note: EXPEL baseline (which also uses experiential insights) underperforms here, and the paper attributes its method's gains partly to the trainable utility weighting over these success/failure-contrasted strategies.
memory_evolution_update: link-and-evolve with dedup-merge and prune: when a new path is generated the agent reinforces existing principles (UpdateConfidence), creates new meta-cognition nodes for novel patterns (FindMatchingMetaCognition then CreateNewMetaCognitionNode), and discards redundant/low-confidence paths; a quantity cap (~30 meta-cognitions) makes the system prefer UPDATE over CREATE and target low-confidence nodes once the budget is exceeded. Separately, edge weights are continuously refined by REINFORCE (delta-update of utility). So the store is curated/evolving (not purely append-only).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Yes. Meta-cognition selection is a learned, RL-optimized policy over the graph: a stochastic selection p(m_k|q_new) proportional to exp(rho) where rho aggregates trainable edge weights w_qt, w_tm; these weights are optimized by REINFORCE using counterfactual reward gaps (Delta R_k). This is explicitly a policy-gradient-trained retrieval/selection mechanism, not a fixed similarity-only top-k (the no-weight-update ablation confirms the learned weighting is crucial).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Single-agent private memory (no multi-agent sharing). However, the memory graph is shown to be model-agnostic / portable across LLM backends and APIs: a graph constructed with one builder LLM (GPT-4o) transfers to another (Gemini-2.5-pro) and to different downstream policies (Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B) with minor performance differences (Cross-API Robustness, Table 4). This is plug-and-play across frameworks/backbones rather than collective multi-agent memory.
benchmarks: Seven QA datasets. General/open-domain factoid QA: Natural Questions (NQ), TriviaQA, PopQA. Multi-hop QA: HotpotQA (the single in-domain dataset; used for memory construction, graph-weight training, and RL training), 2WikiMultiHopQA (2wiki), MuSiQue, Bamboogle. External knowledge source: 2018 Wikipedia dump with the E5 retriever (exposed as an MCP RAG tool, max 6 tool calls). Backbones: Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B; memory-builder LLMs: GPT-4o (default) and Gemini-2.5-pro (robustness).
benchmark_family: QA and multi-hop QA (single-turn factoid + multi-hop reasoning). No web/embodied/tool-retrieval-leaderboard/code/decision-RL benchmarks; all evaluation is tool-augmented open-domain QA over Wikipedia.
baselines: Inference (zero-training) baselines: ITR/TIR (Tool-Integrated Reasoning, the no-memory tool-use base from RL-Factory/Chai et al. 2025; also written 'ITR' in tables), Direct Inference, CoT (Chain-of-Thought), Direct Trajectory (past trajectories used directly as memory), A-MEM (Xu et al. 2025, dynamic agentic memory notes / graph), EXPEL (Zhao et al. 2024, high-level experiential insights). RL-training baselines: Search-R1 (Jin et al. 2025, multi-turn tool-use RL with no memory) and Search-R1 + memory variants (Direct Trajectory, A-MEM, EXPEL). Cross-API robustness compares the method built with GPT-4o vs Gemini-2.5-pro.
key_metrics: Exact Match (EM) accuracy is the single primary metric, reported per dataset and as a seven-dataset average, plus relative improvement (%) over the relevant base (ITR for inference, Search-R1 for RL). RL training also reports convergence/training curves (Figure 3). No Recall@k/nDCG/F1/latency metrics for the strategy memory itself.
headline_result: The trainable graph memory consistently improves over all memory and no-memory baselines, with gains largest on smaller models. Inference (Table 1): average EM 0.365 on Qwen3-8B (+9.3% rel. over ITR 0.334, best among all methods) and 0.351 on Qwen3-4B (+25.8% rel. over ITR 0.279). RL training (Table 2): average EM 0.408 on Qwen3-8B (+3.29% over Search-R1 0.395) and 0.426 on Qwen3-4B (+13.60% over Search-R1 0.375); notably the trained Qwen3-4B (0.426) exceeds the baseline Qwen3-8B (0.395). Strong out-of-domain generalization despite memory built ONLY from in-domain HotpotQA. Most-cited single number: +25.8% relative average improvement over ITR on Qwen3-4B at inference.
ablations: (1) Disabling weight optimization (Fig.4a/b): freezing edges to uniform weight and retrieving by structural presence only causes a significant performance drop, especially on 2WikiMultiHopQA, validating the REINFORCE-based utility learning. (2) Number of meta-cognitions k (Fig.4c, Table 3, Qwen3-4B avg over 7 datasets): ITR(k=0)=0.279 -> top_k=1=0.344 -> top_k=3=0.351 -> top_k=5=0.355; even a single strategy helps markedly (Bamboogle +11.6%, HotpotQA +2.9%); diminishing returns / noise beyond moderate k, main text recommends k=3 (appendix marginally favors k=5). (3) Cross-API memory robustness (Table 4): memory built with GPT-4o vs Gemini-2.5-pro yields near-identical downstream EM (e.g. Qwen3-8B avg 0.365 vs 0.369; Gemini slightly better, +0.043 on Bamboogle for 8B), showing the framework is largely model-agnostic. (Stated three ablation dimensions: weight updates, number of meta-cognitions, and memory composition granularity/API-call structure.)
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task EM (and relative improvements) are reported; there are no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k, nDCG, retrieval completeness) for the meta-cognition selection. The closest decoupled signal is the k-ablation on number of injected meta-cognitions and the weight-freezing ablation.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Predominantly outcome-only (Exact Match). Some process-oriented signals are reported qualitatively/indirectly: RL training/convergence curves (Figure 3) indicate faster/better convergence, the FSM decision-path abstraction and case studies illustrate trajectory/reasoning quality (e.g. self-checking correcting 'National Security Law' -> 'Macau National Security Law'), but no quantitative step-wise process metrics (e.g. step success rate, faithfulness scores) are given.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported qualitatively as efficiency gains rather than detailed cost accounting. The method accelerates RL convergence (training curves) and yields better final performance; a key efficiency claim is parameter/compute efficiency: a memory-augmented Qwen3-4B (0.426) surpasses a no-memory Qwen3-8B (0.395). Prompt-budget tradeoff is acknowledged: more meta-cognitions add tokens/noise with diminishing returns, so a small k (=3) balances guidance vs prompt cost. No explicit token-count, latency, or API-cost numbers for the memory pipeline are reported; tool calls capped at K=6, GRPO n=8 rollouts, 8x A100. [uncertain on precise compute/token costs]
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed small-k selection: top-k meta-cognitions prepended to the query, k a tuned hyperparameter (k=3 recommended in main text; top_k in {0,1,3,5} ablated, 5 marginally best on 4B average). Meta-cognition pool capped at ~30 nodes (quantity-management in the induction prompt). Agent factual tool calls capped at 6 per query; RAG returns top-3 documents by default. No adaptive/precision-driven k beyond the fixed top-k with the ~30-node memory cap.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses seven existing QA benchmarks: NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue, Bamboogle. Memory built from 1,000 HotpotQA examples; graph weights trained on 5,000 HotpotQA examples; remaining HotpotQA training split used as RL corpus. No new benchmark constructed.)
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes (similarity-activated subgraph + learned-weight top-k meta-cognition selection), Reuse: yes (selected strategies verbalized and prepended to guide acting and RL), Revise: partial (meta-cognitions are induced/updated by contrasting success vs failure FSM paths and confidence updates; no per-instance verbatim-then-edit case adaptation), Retain: yes (new/updated meta-cognition nodes and reinforced edge weights retained in the graph during construction; redundant/low-confidence paths pruned)].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work frames itself as agent memory / experiential learning / meta-cognition + RL, and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner or use the term 'case-based reasoning'. It realizes CBR-like Retrieve/Reuse/Retain mechanisms under a trainable-graph-memory and implicit-vs-explicit-memory framing (related to Reflexion, ExpeL, A-MEM, G-Memory).
tool_document_engineering: N/A (not a tool-retrieval method; the agent uses a single Wikipedia RAG MCP tool, not a retrievable tool/API index. Memory items are distilled strategy text, not tool docstrings.)
index_content_separation: Partial: the multi-layer graph separates a lightweight high-level meta-cognition layer (retrieved/injected) from heavier underlying query nodes (full trajectories/outcomes) and FSM transition-path nodes (kept for analysis/induction but not injected). However, this is hierarchical abstraction rather than an explicit progressive-disclosure 'index-then-load-content' retrieval mechanism.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: The factual retrieval is wrapped as a modular MCP tool (search-query_rag) the LLM invokes autonomously (function-calling protocol via <tool_call>/<tool_response> tags over the 2018 Wikipedia dump with E5). The strategy memory graph itself is an internally-managed store, not a live external tool registry; no RapidAPI/RESTful CRUD auto-sync. So: function-calling/MCP for the knowledge tool, internal graph for strategy memory.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (single search tool; no inter-tool dependency modeling).
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted distillation + RL utility calibration rather than per-case verbatim reuse: retrieved meta-cognitions are reused as injected guidance (not copied solutions to edit). New strategies are produced by an LLM that contrasts success vs failure FSM paths (intra-query), borrows from similar successful queries (inter-query speculative), or distills from positive examples; the graph's edge weights are then adapted by REINFORCE on counterfactual reward, and the downstream policy is fine-tuned via GRPO under the augmented context.
builds_on: RL-Factory (Chai et al. 2025) plug-and-play multi-turn tool-use RL framework and its TIR/ITR base; Search-R1 (Jin et al. 2025) as the RL search-agent baseline extended; GRPO for policy optimization; ReAct (Yao et al. 2022) think/act tool interleaving; experiential-memory line — Reflexion (Zhang/Shinn et al. 2023), ExpeL (Zhao et al. 2024), A-MEM (Xu et al. 2025); graph-memory line — G-Memory (Zhang et al. 2025), Zep (Rasmussen et al. 2025), HopRAG (Liu et al. 2025); heterogeneous graph neural networks (Zhang et al. 2019) for the weighted-graph formalism; E5 embeddings (Wang et al. 2024) and DPR/2018 Wikipedia (Karpukhin et al. 2020) for the search tool; long-horizon memory agents MEM1 (Zhou et al. 2025), MemAgent (Yu et al. 2025).
contrasts_with: Implicit memory via training (RL-only, e.g. Search-R1) — generalizes but is black-box, lossy, and prone to catastrophic forgetting; and explicit memory via static prompting (Direct Trajectory, A-MEM, EXPEL, Mem0, and static/logic-aware graph memories like Zep/HopRAG/G-Memory) — interpretable but non-adaptive and poorly generalizing, with no mechanism to evaluate/refine strategy utility. EXPEL in particular (raw experiential insights, inference-only) underperforms and even degrades RL training in their tables (-6.08% on 8B, -10.13% on 4B vs Search-R1). The paper positions its trainable, utility-aware graph injected INTO the RL training loop against all of these inference-only or static-weight approaches.
lineage: Group F (decision/memory + RL): a 2025 method that fuses experiential graph memory with RL training for tool-augmented decision-making. It advances the Reflexion -> ExpeL -> A-MEM / G-Memory experiential- and graph-memory lineage by (a) abstracting trajectories into canonical FSM decision paths and distilling human-interpretable meta-cognitions in a multi-layer heterogeneous graph, (b) making memory TRAINABLE via REINFORCE on counterfactual reward gaps (utility-aware edge weights / learned selection policy), and (c) integrating the retrieved strategies into the GRPO RL training loop as an explicit policy prior (not inference-only), thereby unifying explicit (interpretable) and implicit (parametric) memory.
